0x61b4840.name: rocksdb::TracerHelper::ParseTraceHeader
quirks: The split loop runs exactly three times with a 32-bit position: when std::string::find returns npos, pos becomes (npos + 1) & 0xFFFFFFFF == 0, so the next iteration searches from the payload start again. A one-TAB payload's third field is the payload's own first field; a no-TAB payload repeats itself three times. The split loop's own out_of_range check (pos > size) is present in the binary but unreachable: pos is a found TAB index + 1, or 0 after the wrap.

The 15/17-byte skips are offsets only: the label bytes 'Trace Version: ' / 'RocksDB Version: ' are never compared. The producer (Tracer::WriteHeader, 0x61b3860) writes exactly those labels -- .rodata 0x4478de and 0x442aec -- which is why the offsets are 15 and 17.

The returned Status is the SECOND ParseVersionStr status: it is moved over the first one in the out Status (freeing the first one's state; the first one is OK whenever the second call runs, so nothing is freed in practice). The first call's error short-circuits before the second call: the binary tests only the low byte of the returned code.

ParseVersionStr writes its version int only on success; on failure the caller's out-parameter is untouched. So on a first-version failure both versions are untouched; on a second-version failure the trace version is written and the RocksDB version is not.
rules: split trace.payload (std::string at Trace+0x18) on TAB (single byte 0x09, .rodata 0x43fc29, find with n=1) into exactly three fields; each field is payload[pos : pos+len] with len = distance to the next TAB or the remainder

field[1].substr(15) -- throws std::out_of_range ('basic_string::substr', .rodata 0x43e542; format '%s: __pos (which is %zu) > this->size() (which is %zu)', .rodata 0x958cf8) when field[1] is shorter than 15
field[2].substr(17) -- throws the same way when field[2] is shorter than 17
status1, *trace_version = ParseVersionStr(field[1][15:]); if status1 is not OK, return status1 at once
status2, *rocksdb_version = ParseVersionStr(field[2][17:]); return status2 (it overwrites status1 in the out Status)
field[0] is never read (it holds the 16-byte magic in live headers, but nothing in this function checks it)
